artworks.title: Rudolf II as Vertumnus
artworks.description: Arcimboldo's Skokloster masterpiece: Emperor Rudolf II as a composite of fruit and vegetables — Vertumnus as the season-god emperor, the most famous face the Roman orchard god ever wore.

artworks.title: Vertumnus and Pomona
artworks.description: Pontormo's Poggio a Caiano fresco: Vertumnus among Medici orchard abundance — Ovid's shape-shifting wooer woven into villa propaganda.

artworks.title: Vertumnus and Pomona
artworks.description: Melzi's Berlin panel: Vertumnus in crone disguise wooing Pomona — Leonardo's pupil turning Metamorphoses 14 into Lombard grace.

artworks.title: Vertumnus and Pomona
artworks.description: Rubens for the Torre de la Parada: Vertumnus sheds the old-woman mask before Pomona — Flemish flesh for the god of seasonal change.

artworks.title: Landscape with Vertumnus and Pomona
artworks.description: Bloemaert nests the orchard courtship in a Dutch world landscape — Vertumnus persuading as Pomona listens. Yale University Art Gallery.

popCulture.title: Metamorphoses
popCulture.creator: Ovid
popCulture.description: Book XIV — Vertumnus' disguises and the final unveiling before Pomona: the canonical orchard romance.

popCulture.title: Vertumnus
popCulture.description: Roman god of seasons and plant growth — Arcimboldo's fruit-face emperor and Ovid's shape-shifting wooer of Pomona.
